name: Tauranga
note: Town: the Bay of Plenty's only city, a base with harbour, waterfront and Mount Maunganui nearby.

name: Mount Maunganui
note: Town: beachside suburb and holiday town at the mouth of Tauranga Harbour, 'The Mount', a base for the beach and Mauao.

name: Rotorua
note: City: geothermal and Māori-culture city and lakes base, a major tourist centre.

name: Whakatāne
note: Town: coastal town and base for Ōhope, Whale Island and Whirinaki, one of the sunniest in NZ.

name: Ōpōtiki
note: Town: eastern coastal town and gateway to the Motu Trail, Waioeka Gorge and East Cape.

name: Te Puke
note: Town: horticultural centre south-east of Tauranga, kiwifruit country.

name: Waihi Beach
note: Town: small beach town at the western end of the Bay with a 9 km white-sand beach.

name: Katikati
note: Town: small town on the western Bay, base for the Bird Gardens and Kaimai walks; named in no visitor list read so far.

name: Kawerau
note: Town: mill town and base for the Tarawera Forest permits (the DOC page sends visitors to the Kawerau i-SITE). No visitor guide chapter found.

name: Ōmokoroa
note: Settlement: coastal peninsula settlement 20 km north-west of Tauranga with a cycleway and walks.

name: Te Puna
note: Settlement: village west of Tauranga, a place to eat and relax, named by the tourism board.

name: Pukehina
note: Beach settlement: a long uncrowded surf and wind-sport coast with an estuary on the other side, named by the tourism board.

name: Maketū
note: Settlement: seaside settlement and historic landing place of a waka, with sandy inlet and cliffed coastline, named by the tourism board and Te Puke's Wikivoyage page.

name: The Elms
note: Historic site: 1847 missionary station, now Te Papa Tauranga, with a garden and guided house tour (entry charge).

name: Gate Pā
note: Historic site: battlefield of the 1864 Battle of Pukehinahina, a New Zealand Wars site visitors can walk.

name: Mission Cemetery
note: Historic site: early cemetery near The Elms named by the tourism board among significant sites.

name: Durham Redoubt
note: Historic site: New Zealand Wars redoubt near The Elms, named by the tourism board.

name: Monmouth Redoubt
note: Historic site: New Zealand Wars redoubt near The Elms, named by the tourism board.

name: Tauranga Art Gallery
note: Museum: regional public art gallery in the CBD with contemporary exhibitions (free for NZ residents).

name: Southern Waterfront Boardwalk
note: Walk: boardwalk along the southern Tauranga waterfront with harbour views and marine life, named by the tourism board.

name: Marshalls Animal Park
note: Wildlife park: farm animal park with horses, deer and farm animals, at McLaren Falls Road.

name: Katikati Bird Gardens
note: Gardens: formal and wetland gardens on the inner harbour with native birds including kea, a café and golf-cart tours.

name: Te Puna Quarry Park
note: Park: former quarry turned into a volunteer-built park, free to visit.

name: McLaren Falls Park
note: Park: 190 ha park beside Lake McLaren with walking tracks, trout fishing, disc golf and the glow-worm Waterfall Track.

name: Kaiate Falls
note: Waterfall: waterfall near Tauranga listed by Wikivoyage among its falls.

name: Whataroa Falls
note: Waterfall: waterfall in the Tauranga region named by Wikivoyage.

name: Omanawa Falls
note: Waterfall: waterfall in the Tauranga region named by Wikivoyage.

name: Wairere Falls
note: Waterfall: 153 m waterfall in the Kaimai Range reached by a DOC track; Wikivoyage names it among the Tauranga falls.

name: Mauao
note: Mountain: volcanic peak at the harbour mouth with summit and base tracks and views over the Bay (a historic reserve).

name: Mount Maunganui Main Beach
note: Beach: surf beach on the Mount Maunganui peninsula, the 'Surf City' beach, patrolled in summer.

name: Pilot Bay
note: Beach: calm harbour-side bay on the Mount peninsula, popular for paddleboarding, with sunset cruise-ship views.

name: Tauranga Harbour
note: Harbour: large harbour around which Tauranga is built, a place for fishing, kayaking and boat trips.

name: Matakana Island
note: Island: long coastal island off Tauranga with orchards, farmland and pine forest, the largest coastal island in the Bay.

name: Tūhua (Mayor Island)
note: Island: dormant volcano 35 km offshore, a wildlife refuge with a marine reserve, visits by pre-arranged permission only.

name: Motiti Island
note: Island: inhabited island 21 km north-east of Tauranga, named by the tourism board as seen from boat cruises; visitors are asked not to land.

name: Papamoa Beach
note: Beach: surf and swim beach east of Mount Maunganui; Wikivoyage Te Puke names Papamoa beaches as a swim stop.

name: Papamoa Hills Regional Park
note: Park: regional park of tracks in the Papamoa hills; no visitor guide found naming it.

name: Comvita Honey Tour
note: Visitor attraction: tour of the Comvita manuka honey and health-product factory with a visitor centre near Paengaroa (operator tour).

name: Kiwifruit Country
note: Farm attraction: kiwifruit orchard tours and wine tasting at Paengaroa.

name: Golf Te Puke
note: Golf course: 18-hole public course south of Te Puke (operator, not a visitor attraction in the usual sense).

name: Orokawa Bay
note: Beach/bay: pohutukawa-lined bay reached by a walk from the north end of Waihi Beach, with a detour to William Wright Falls.

name: William Wright Falls
note: Waterfall: 28 m waterfall on the Orokawa Bay walk, a 45-minute detour.

name: Orokawa Scenic Reserve
note: Reserve: scenic reserve north of Waihi Beach containing Orokawa Bay and William Wright Falls tracks.

name: Athenree Hot Springs
note: Hot pools: two outdoor hot-spring pools near Waihi Beach (entry fee).

name: Owharoa Falls
note: Waterfall: waterfall in the Kaimai-Mamaku park near Waihi, reached by a DOC track.

name: Karangahake Gorge
note: Historic gorge: gold-mining remains and river walkways (the Karangahake Windows walk), reached by DOC walks.

name: Karangahake Windows Walk
note: Walk: historic gorge walk through old mining tunnels and past the Windows, a DOC track.

name: Victoria Battery
note: Historic site: restored gold-stamping battery site in Karangahake Gorge, named by DOC.

name: Waihi-Waikino Goldfields Railway
note: Heritage railway: restored tramway between Waihi and Waikino; the ride is the attraction, no destination-station summary found in a visitor source.

name: Kaimai-Mamaku Conservation Park
note: Park: conservation park between Karangahake and near Rotorua with historic mining and kauri sites and popular tramping tracks.

name: Aongatete Nature Trail
note: Walk: short nature trail near Katikati within the Kaimai-Mamaku park, a DOC track.

name: Kaimai Heritage Trail
note: Walk: heritage tramline and mining trail through the Kaimai park, a DOC track.

name: Kaimai Summit Loop Track
note: Walk: summit loop track in the Kaimai Range, a DOC track.

name: Te Aroha Summit Track
note: Walk: summit track on Te Aroha in the Kaimai-Mamaku park, a DOC track.

name: Kaharoa Conservation Area
note: Conservation area: forest home of the endangered kōkako, with the Kōkako Track to Onaia Stream.

name: Otanewainuku Forest
note: Forest: native forest with giant trees and birdlife, with a lookout track and a rimu loop walk.

name: Mangorewa Ecological Area
note: Walk: day tramp through dense forest between two streams, the Mangorewa Track (DOC), also named by Wikivoyage Rotorua.

name: Matatā Lagoon
note: Coastal area: lagoon, wildlife refuge, campsite and short walk at Matatā, good for swimming and fishing.

name: Ōhiwa Harbour
note: Harbour: harbour near Ōpōtiki and Whakatāne, sea kayak tours and birdlife, named by Wikivoyage Whakatāne.

name: Whakatāne Library and Exhibition Centre
note: Civic building: town library with exhibition galleries and changing shows (donation); a civic building.

name: Whakatāne Gardens
note: Park: town park with a rose garden and a Japanese garden.

name: Diveworks Dolphin and Seal Encounters
note: Operator: four-hour dolphin and seal watching trips around White and Whale Islands (a DOC concessionaire; operator, not a place).

name: KG Kayaks
note: Operator: guided kayak tours to Whale Island and Ōhiwa Harbour (operator, not a place).

name: Moutohorā (Whale Island)
note: Island: native wildlife sanctuary with birds, New Zealand fur seals and a geothermal hot-water beach, reached by boat tour.

name: Ōhope Beach
note: Beach: 6 km town beach for swimming, surfing and beach activities at Ōhope, near Whakatāne.

name: Ōhope Scenic Reserve
note: Reserve: scenic reserve at Ōhope with coastal and bush walks, named by DOC.

name: Nga Tapuwae o Toi Walkway
note: Walk: 16 km loop from Whakatāne to Ōhope through coast and bush with historic pā sites (5–7 hours).

name: Tauwhare Pā Scenic Reserve
note: Historic reserve: pā site with a short walk, named by DOC.

name: White Pine Bush Track
note: Walk: bush walk near Whakatāne, a DOC track.

name: White Island (Whakaari)
note: Volcanic island: active volcano 50 km offshore visited by tour and seen on scenic flights; closed to visitors since the 2019 eruption at the time of this run.

name: Te Paepae o Aotea (Volkner Rocks) Marine Reserve
wiki: Te Paepae o Aotea (Volkner Rocks) Marine Reserve
coordinates_source: wikipedia:Te Paepae o Aotea (Volkner Rocks) Marine Reserve
note: Marine reserve: diving and snorkelling reserve off Whakatāne's coast with rich marine life, named by DOC.

name: Ōpōtiki Museum
note: Museum: local museum on Church Street, open weekdays and Saturday morning.

name: Opotiki Rodeo
note: Annual event: rodeo held every December at War Memorial Park; an annual event, not a permanent place.

name: Waiotahi Beach
note: Beach: patrolled beach 5–10 minutes west of Ōpōtiki, for swimming, fishing and relaxing.

name: Motu River Jet Boat Tours
note: Operator: jet-boat tours on the Motu River east of Ōpōtiki (operator; the river is the place).

name: Hukutaia Domain
note: Reserve: 4.5 ha native forest with short tracks past Taketakerau, a puriri tree estimated over 2000 years old.

name: Motu Trail
note: Cycle trail: 19–93 km Great Ride between Matawai and Ōpōtiki with the Dunes Trail near Ōpōtiki and the Pakihi track.

name: Tirohanga Dunes Trail
note: Walk: easy dune trail near Ōpōtiki, part of the Motu Trail system, named by DOC.

name: Pakihi Track
note: Walk: remote wilderness cycle and walking track on the Motu Trail, named by DOC.

name: Waioeka Gorge Scenic Reserve
note: Reserve: gorge scenic reserve on SH2 between Ōpōtiki and Gisborne with the Tauranga Loop and Manganuku tracks.

name: Kuirau Park
note: Park: free city park with boiling mud pools and footbaths in central Rotorua, open 24 hours.

name: Government Gardens
note: Park: formal gardens near the CBD with the Blue Baths and the Rotorua Museum.

name: Blue Baths
note: Historic building: 1933 Art Deco bathhouse in Government Gardens (heritage building with a public pool).

name: Rotorua Museum
note: Museum: city museum in Government Gardens, closed since 2016 after an earthquake, reopening pending.

name: Sulphur Bay (Motutara)
note: Walkway: boardwalk past hot springs and sulphur vents on Lake Rotorua's south-east shore with waterbirds; named as Motutara in Wikivoyage.

name: Te Puia
note: Geothermal park and Māori arts institute at Whakarewarewa: paid day pass, guided tours, geysers and a kiwi conservation centre. Wikipedia title redirects to a different village (Te Puia Springs), so views are set to 0.

name: Whakarewarewa Thermal Village
note: Cultural village: living Māori village with geothermal features and self-guided or guided walks (paid).

name: Pōhutu Geyser
note: Geyser: geyser in the Whakarewarewa thermal valley at Te Puia, with a daily eruption (Wikipedia only, no visitor guide found).

name: Waimangu Volcanic Valley
note: Geothermal valley: valley formed by the 1886 Mount Tarawera eruption, with walks and a boat cruise on Lake Rotomahana (paid).

name: Wai-O-Tapu Thermal Wonderland
note: Geothermal park: coloured craters and pools, with the Lady Knox Geyser erupting daily (paid; listed as closed for renovation in Wikivoyage).

name: Lady Knox Geyser
note: Geyser: geyser at Wai-O-Tapu that erupts daily on a timed schedule.

name: Champagne Pool
note: Hot pool: large acid hot pool at Wai-O-Tapu; a feature of Wai-O-Tapu, named by Wikipedia only.

name: Buried Village (Te Wairoa)
note: Historic site: village buried by the 1886 Mount Tarawera eruption, with a museum and guided tour (paid).

name: Agrodome
note: Farm attraction: farm show with sheep, alpacas and farm tours, with the National Kiwi Hatchery on site (paid).

name: National Kiwi Hatchery
note: Wildlife attraction: kiwi hatchery at the Agrodome site offering visits during hatching season.

name: Wingspan National Bird of Prey Centre
wiki: Wingspan National Bird of Prey Centre
note: Wildlife centre: bird-of-prey centre with a daily flight display, including the endangered kārearea falcon (paid).

name: aMaze Me
note: Attraction: 1.4 km hedge maze on Paradise Valley Road (paid).

name: Skyline Rotorua
note: Gondola: gondola ride up Mount Ngongotaha with panoramic views of Rotorua (operator; the summit is the viewpoint).

name: Mount Ngongotaha
note: Mountain: mountain and scenic reserve above Rotorua with a rata tree walk and the Jubilee Track, reached by gondola or on foot.

name: Polynesian Spa
note: Hot-pool spa: 26 hot mineral pools on the lake shore with spa therapies (paid).

name: Kerosene Creek
note: Hot stream: naturally hot stream (about 37 °C) for open-air bathing south of Rotorua; Wikivoyage warns of thefts.

name: Waikite Valley Thermal Pools
note: Hot pools: natural geothermal thermal pools in Waikite Valley (paid).

name: Twin Streams (The Bridge)
note: Bathing spot: open-air hot and cold streams that meet at the southern end of Waiotapu Loop Road.

name: Hamurana Springs
note: Springs: spring-fed reserve on the north-east shore of Lake Rotorua, named by Wikipedia; no visitor guide found.

name: Hell's Gate (Tikitere)
note: Geothermal park: geothermal reserve with mud pools, hot springs and a mud bath spa, named by Wikipedia; no visitor guide chapter found in this run.

name: Orakei Korako
note: Geothermal park: geothermal valley on the Waikato River with terraces and a cave (paid); named by Wikipedia only in this run.

name: Okere Falls
note: Waterfall: Kaituna River falls at the outflow of Lake Rotoiti, a rafting and short-walk stop, with a Māori cultural site.

name: Rotorua Walkway
note: Walk: 26 km walkway around Rotorua linking the parks, Redwoods and the Government Gardens (a council brochure is the guide).

name: Redwoods Forest
note: Forest: 6 ha grove of planted redwoods in Whakarewarewa Forest with mountain-bike trails and walks.

name: Whakarewarewa Forest
note: Forest park: state forest park with 60 km of mountain-bike tracks and walks, named by DOC.

name: Rainbow Mountain (Maunga Kākaramea)
note: Mountain: summit walk with views over the plains south of Rotorua, part of Maunga Kākaramea and Waiotapu scenic reserves; Wikivoyage names it Rainbow Mountain.

name: Waiotapu Boardwalk
note: Walk: boardwalk past geothermal features in the Waiotapu scenic reserve, a DOC track.

name: Maunga Kākaramea Crater Lake Walk
note: Walk: crater lake walk on Maunga Kākaramea, a DOC track.

name: Lake Rotorua
note: Lake: the lake that gives Rotorua its name, with a lakefront promenade, scenic flights, amphibious tours and trout fishing.

name: Mokoia Island
note: Island: island in Lake Rotorua reached by boat tour, with a walk and historic Māori sites.

name: Lake Tarawera
note: Lake: lake at the foot of Mount Tarawera with campsites, walks, and the Tarawera Falls track.

name: Tarawera Falls
note: Waterfall: waterfall reached by the Tarawera Falls track through the Tarawera forest (permit required by road).

name: Mount Tarawera
note: Volcano: volcano that erupted in 1886, seen from the Buried Village and Lake Tarawera; named by Wikipedia.

name: Lake Ōkataina
note: Lake: lake with walking tracks and mountain-bike routes in the Okataina scenic reserve.

name: Lake Tikitapu (Blue Lake)
note: Lake: Blue Lake, popular for swimming and water sports, with an easy walking track around it.

name: Lake Ōkareka
note: Lake: quiet lake with camping, mistletoe walks and short tracks.

name: Lake Rotoiti
note: Lake: lake with forest walks and lakeside picnic and swimming spots, at the Okere Falls end of the lakes.

name: Lake Rotoma
note: Lake: lake reached by forest walk and the Rotoma Bridle Track, with swimming and picnicking.

name: Lake Rotomahana
note: Lake: lake whose boat cruise is part of Waimangu's visit; named by Wikipedia only.

name: Lake Rotokākahi (Green Lake)
note: Lake: Green Lake near Lake Tikitapu, named by Wikipedia; no visitor guide found in this run.

name: Lake Rerewhakaaitu
note: Lake: recreation reserve lake with campsites near Rotorua, named by DOC.

name: Kaharoa Kōkako Track
note: Walk: forest track in the Kaharoa conservation area, the kōkako track, a DOC track.

name: Lake Waikareiti
note: Lake: lake in Te Urewera reached by a walk from Lake Waikaremoana, named by DOC.

name: Lake Waikaremoana
note: Lake: large lake in Te Urewera with a Great Walk, short walks and huts (DOC).

name: Lake Waikaremoana Great Walk
note: Great Walk: 46 km multi-day track around Lake Waikaremoana, one of the Great Walks (DOC).

name: Panekire Bluffs
note: Walk: lookout bluffs above Lake Waikaremoana, a DOC track.

name: Lake Kaitawa Fairy Springs Track
note: Walk: track to Fairy Springs near Lake Kaitawa in Te Urewera, a DOC track.

name: Ruapani Circuit Track
note: Walk: circuit track around Lake Ruapani in Te Urewera, a DOC track.

name: Te Urewera National Park
note: Park: national park of forest and lakes, home of the Tūhoe people, with Lake Waikaremoana at its heart.

name: Te Urewera Visitor Centre at Te Kura Whenua
note: Visitor centre: information centre at Te Kura Whenua, Lake Waikaremoana; an information building, not a visitor attraction on its own.

name: Whirinaki Te Pua-a-Tāne Conservation Park
note: Park: conservation park of podocarp forest with tramping tracks and a recreation camp (DOC).

name: Whirinaki Track
note: Walk: tramping track in the Whirinaki park, a DOC track.

name: Waiatiu Falls Track
note: Waterfall: waterfall walk in the Whirinaki park, a DOC track.

name: Te Pua-a-Tāne Circuit
note: Walk: circuit track in the Whirinaki park, a DOC track.
